questions.question: What happens to light speed when it enters glass from air?
questions.explanation: Light slows down in glass compared to air because glass has a higher refractive index.

questions.question: Which surface scatters light in many directions?
questions.explanation: A rough surface causes diffuse reflection, scattering light in many directions. Smooth surfaces reflect light in a single direction.

questions.question: Total internal reflection occurs when light:

choices.A: Goes from slower to faster medium at small angle
choices.B: Goes from faster to slower medium above critical angle

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection happens when light in a higher-speed medium (like water to air) hits the boundary above the critical angle and reflects entirely.
steps: Choose faster to slower above critical
questions.fastStrategy: Inside-to-air, big angle → total internal reflection.

questions.question: Which wave behavior explains hearing sound around a corner?
questions.explanation: Sound bends and spreads around obstacles through diffraction, allowing you to hear around corners.
steps: Reflection needs a surface, refraction a medium change

questions.question: Which statement about light in vacuum is correct?

choices.B: Speed is the same for all colors

questions.explanation: In vacuum, all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed c. Speed differences by color occur only in media.
steps: Color affects speed only in materials
questions.fastStrategy: In vacuum, all light shares speed c.

questions.question: What does a prism do to white light?
questions.explanation: A prism refracts different wavelengths by different amounts, dispersing white light into a spectrum of colors.
questions.fastStrategy: Prism spreads white light into colors (dispersion).

questions.question: What happens to wave frequency when it enters a new medium?
questions.explanation: Frequency of a wave stays the same across media; wavelength and speed change instead.
steps: At boundary, speed and λ can change
questions.fastStrategy: Wave crosses boundary: f fixed, λ and v adjust.

questions.question: Which term describes the bending of waves around obstacles?
questions.explanation: Diffraction is bending/spreading of waves around edges or openings.

questions.question: If frequency of a sound wave increases, its pitch is perceived as:
questions.explanation: Higher frequency sound corresponds to higher pitch.

questions.question: Which EM waves have the longest wavelengths?
questions.explanation: Radio waves occupy the long-wavelength, low-frequency end of the electromagnetic spectrum.
questions.fastStrategy: EM spectrum: radio longest λ; gamma shortest λ.

questions.question: Which EM waves have the shortest wavelengths?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are at the high-frequency, short-wavelength end of the spectrum.
steps: Spectrum order places gamma at shortest λ
questions.fastStrategy: Shortest λ, highest f → gamma rays.

questions.question: Ultraviolet light has a frequency that is:
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet lies just above visible light in frequency (shorter wavelength).
questions.fastStrategy: UV is above visible; IR/microwave below.

questions.question: Infrared radiation is mainly associated with:
questions.explanation: Warm objects emit infrared radiation, often associated with heat transfer.

questions.question: Which property stays constant for light when passing from air to water?
questions.explanation: Frequency stays the same across boundaries; speed and wavelength change, direction may bend.
steps: New medium changes speed and λ
questions.fastStrategy: At boundaries: frequency fixed, v and λ shift.

questions.question: Light that bounces off a surface is undergoing:
questions.explanation: Bouncing off a surface is reflection. Refraction is bending through; diffraction is spreading; polarization filters vibrations.
steps: Other terms involve passing or filtering

questions.question: Light passing through a narrow slit and spreading is:
questions.explanation: Spreading after a narrow opening is diffraction. Interference is combining waves, though diffraction often leads to interference patterns.

questions.question: In the visible spectrum, blue light has a ______ wavelength than red light.
questions.explanation: Blue has shorter wavelength and higher frequency than red within the visible range.
questions.fastStrategy: Blue/Violet shorter λ; Red longer λ.

questions.question: When two waves overlap and form a pattern of bright and dark regions, this is:
questions.explanation: Interference results from overlapping waves, creating constructive (bright) and destructive (dark) regions.

questions.question: A longitudinal wave vibrates:
questions.explanation: In longitudinal waves, particle motion is parallel to the direction of wave travel (compressions and rarefactions).

questions.question: What determines the pitch of a sound?
questions.explanation: Pitch corresponds to the frequency of the sound wave. Amplitude affects loudness.

questions.question: If a wave's period is 0.5 seconds, its frequency is:
questions.explanation: Frequency f = 1/T. With T = 0.5 s, f = 1 / 0.5 = 2 Hz.

questions.question: If the period of a wave doubles, the frequency:
questions.explanation: Since f = 1/T, doubling period halves frequency.

questions.question: Which wave property is most closely related to energy carried by a wave?
questions.explanation: For many waves (like light intensity and sound loudness), greater amplitude corresponds to more energy.

questions.question: What property of light changes when it enters a denser medium?
questions.explanation: Frequency stays the same; speed decreases in a denser medium. Wavelength changes accordingly.
questions.fastStrategy: Light slows in denser media; f constant.

questions.question: The part of the EM spectrum used for cell phones is mainly:
questions.explanation: Cell phones primarily use microwave frequencies (a subset of radio waves).
questions.fastStrategy: Cell signals ride in the microwave/radio band.
